tex_content.label: eq:polygon-length
tex_content.html:
\begin{equation} \operatorname {Length}(P_\gamma )= \sum _{j=0}^{N-1}(2\pi /N)\, \operatorname {speed}(P_\gamma |_{[2\pi j/N,2\pi (j+1)/N]}). \end{equation} For a pointwise null family, the raw polygons have genuine filling disks and filling-area error less than $\zeta $. Fixed-profile flattening gives a family smooth in the angular coordinate, with continuous first and second angular jets, freely homotopic to the original family in the $C^1$ loop space. Source: MT20071. Definition 19.182. Claims 19.19–19.203. Corollary 19.21, pp. 450–4514. Lemma 19.175. Claim 19.22, pp. 449–453
Proof

Compactness gives a common geodesically convex neighborhood of the diagonal and uniform continuity of the family’s first angular derivatives. Fine meshes therefore give unique short geodesic sides with uniformly small chord deficits. The interpolation’s transverse derivative tends uniformly to zero, while its angular derivative stays bounded, so its Jacobian area tends uniformly to zero.

Flatten each side using the same smooth increasing transition, flat at its endpoints. This preserves its image and length and matches all angular derivatives at the vertices. A short geodesic homotopy from the original loops to the flattened loops is continuous in $C^1$. The flattening is a circle homeomorphism; absorb it into each disk’s boundary label rather than precomposing its interior by a nonsmooth inverse. Gluing the small interpolation annuli to actual disks in both directions gives the filling-area error.

□
